primary_topics: Keynote address at the World Bank's Philippine Development Innovation Marketplace (Panibagong Paraan 2008), April 9, 2008 -- invited by World Bank Country Director Bert Hofman; theme: Building Partnerships for Local Governance
The innovation: inverting the organizational pyramid -- solving national problems from the base (local governance) going up to the apex, rather than the traditional top-down approach

Six principles for governance innovation: (1) truth and integrity; (2) transparency and accountability; (3) rule of law; (4) responsible citizenship; (5) democratic institutions; (6) visionary leadership by example with specific, quantifiable vision-mission statements

The MVP/PLDT leadership story (third telling): three silent days -- 60 cars reduced to one; advertising commission deposited to company account; arrived before 8 AM; result: market worth multiplied tenfold and 'corporate ethics a hundred fold'
sub_topics: Opening context: CBCP statement that 'we are in the midst of restlessness and confusion, facing a crisis of truth and the pervading cancer of corruption'; Church called for circles of discernment at the grassroots level in parishes and Basic Ecclesial Communities

The Panibagong Paraan innovation: turning the Church's spiritual-discernment approach into a secular governance innovation -- instead of top-down, solve from the base (local governance) going up; 'This great innovation of solving the nation's problems from the base up rather than the traditional direction coming from the top going to the grassroots is itself the big innovation in our marketplace today'

Six principles: (1) Truth and integrity -- 'integrity goes beyond mere honesty or the refusal to tell a falsehood; it is the moral courage to denounce a wrong and to promote the truth'; (2) Transparency and accountability -- 'those who govern must be ready to endure the sunlight and the scrutiny of their public as well as private lives'; (3) Rule of law -- 'reigns when the actions and decisions of government are made and done in accordance with the Constitution and the laws, not pursuant to the wiles and whims of the governors'; (4) Responsible citizenship -- 'being constantly informed of national and community affairs, participating in communal activities, and helping in the transformation of our culture of patronage to a culture of integrity'; (5) Democratic institutions -- 'due process, civilian supremacy, and checks and balances'; (6) Visionary leadership -- 'always start with a vision; a vision-mission statement must be specific and quantifiable, not a mere collection of motherhood principles'

MVP/PLDT story (third telling, with new metric): same three-day silent leadership story; here adds the result: 'the market worth of PLDT multiplied tenfold, and its corporate ethics a hundred fold' -- the first time a quantified outcome is given for the MVP story

Closing message: 'Leadership by personal example of integrity, transparency and accountability, not by mere rhetoric and certainly not by double speak and hypocrisy, must top every innovative proposal to solve every organization's developmental problem and need'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered April 9, 2008 as the keynote at the World Bank's Philippine Development Innovation Marketplace (Panibagong Paraan 2008, theme: Building Partnerships for Local Governance) -- invited by World Bank Country Director Bert Hofman -- this address by CJP opens with the CBCP's statement that the Philippines faces 'a crisis of truth and the pervading cancer of corruption,' with the Church calling for circles of discernment in parishes and Basic Ecclesial Communities. CJP links this to the Panibagong Paraan innovation: instead of the traditional top-down approach, solve governance problems from the base (local communities) going up to the apex -- 'this great innovation of solving the nation's problems from the base up is itself the big innovation in our marketplace today.' He presents six governance principles: (1) truth and integrity ('integrity is the moral courage to denounce a wrong and to promote the truth'); (2) transparency and accountability ('those who govern must endure the sunlight and scrutiny of their public and private lives'); (3) rule of law; (4) responsible citizenship (transforming 'a culture of patronage to a culture of integrity'); (5) democratic institutions (due process, civilian supremacy, checks and balances); (6) visionary leadership ('a vision-mission statement must be specific and quantifiable, not a mere collection of motherhood principles'). He closes with the MVP/PLDT three-day silent leadership story -- in this version with a quantified outcome for the first time: 'the market worth of PLDT multiplied tenfold, and its corporate ethics a hundred fold.' Final message: 'Leadership by personal example of integrity, transparency and accountability, not by mere rhetoric and certainly not by double speak and hypocrisy, must top every innovative proposal to solve every organization's developmental problem and need.'
